speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The Customs Act was last amended in 2018.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These amendments will enable Singapore Customs to more effectively carry out its mandate of trade facilitation and revenue protection and ensure that bad actors are deterred from committing offences under the Customs Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: First, we will give the Director-General of Singapore Customs the power to authorise auxiliary police officers, or APOs, to exercise powers of search, arrest and seizure.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Today, only officers who are directly employed by Singapore Customs can exercise these powers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: However, Singapore Customs also engages APOs to support its enforcement operations, and APOs will need to be granted these powers to perform their duties effectively.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: And this is in line with the practice in other public agencies, such as the Health Sciences Authority, the Land Transport Authority, and the National Environment Agency, who are able to appoint APOs as authorised officers under their respective legislation to exercise similar powers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Second, we will grant Singapore Customs the legal power to require licensees to remove all dutiable goods from licensed warehouses before the expiry or withdrawal of their licences.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Today, the Licensed Warehouse scheme allows licensed companies to store imported dutiable goods in a designated premise known as a Licensed Warehouse, with duty and the Goods and Services Tax on these goods suspended.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: To qualify for this scheme, companies must meet requirements including having good compliance records and ensuring the security of the dutiable goods.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In the absence of any legislative lever today, Singapore Customs has no legal powers to compel these companies to remove their goods when the company’s license expires or is withdrawn.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Hence, the amendment will make it a requirement for licensees to remove all dutiable goods from the warehouse even before the expiry or the withdrawal of their licence, failing which, Singapore Customs will have the legal powers to remove and dispose of all dutiable goods from the warehouse, and recover any costs incurred for the removal and disposal of these goods.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Third, we will provide officers of customs with the power to stop and conduct searches on the belongings of a person that is committing or is reasonably suspected to have committed an offence under the Customs Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Today, officers of customs can only exercise the power of search on persons under three narrowly prescribed conditions: one, when a person is arriving in Singapore; two, when a person is suspected to be in possession of a bribe; and three, when a person has been arrested for an offence under the Customs Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: However, these conditions are too restrictive for situations when officers of customs conduct inland operations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For instance, officers of customs may receive tip-offs of persons suspected to be in possession of and illegally selling duty unpaid cigarettes in a particular part of Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These suspects are not arriving in Singapore, so they do not meet Condition 1 to invoke search; and they are not suspected to be in possession of a bribe, so they do not meet Condition 2.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: As for Condition 3, while an officer of customs can arrest an individual to invoke the power of search, an arrest would be a high signature move which can have a significant impact on the person involved.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In some cases, arresting the individual may not be necessary if the officer wants to first verify whether an offence has been committed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Hence, it is more effective to amend the law to give officers of customs the legal powers to conduct searches before assessing whether an arrest should be made.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: All in all, this amendment will allow Singapore Customs to conduct their inland enforcement operations more effectively.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Fourth, we will grant Singapore Customs the legal power to seize computers or associated devices, mobile communication devices and cash that are reasonably believed to be connected to offences under the Customs Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In the course of enforcement operations and investigations, it may be necessary for officers of customs to seize such devices and cash proceeds as these may be used as evidence to prosecute the offender under the Customs Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: First, we will introduce a new offence provision to penalise individuals who allow their premises or vehicles to be used to commit an offence under the Customs Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This will more effectively deter individuals from committing an offence or taking actions that assist others in the commission of an offence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For example, there have been cases where individuals repeatedly allowed their premises or vehicles to be used by criminal syndicates to store or transport duty unpaid goods.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These individuals then claim innocence by saying that they did not know their actions had helped to facilitate the commission of offences.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: With this amendment, Singapore Customs will be able to take action against such individuals, unless they are able to show that they had exercised due care in respect of the actions in question.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Second, we will also introduce a new offence provision for acts of altering, suppressing, concealing or destroying any books, documents or other records with the intent of obstructing investigations under the Customs Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Today, such acts are considered offences under the Penal Code, but not the Customs Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This means that when officers of Customs encounter such acts, Singapore Customs will need to refer offenders to the Singapore Police Force (SPF) for investigation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Third, we will enhance the penalties for some offences, to strengthen their deterrent effect.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This aligns the maximum fine with that of other similar offences under the Customs Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These efforts will ultimately strengthen Singapore's status as a trusted and thriving trade hub.
